title: The AI Guard decorator for AWS Lambda handlers: prompt and response scanning at the function boundary, default extractors, and block shapes

prose.text: The Lambda decorator guards the function boundary: it sees the event entering the handler and the result leaving it, and nothing the handler does in between. {{boundary}}

prose.label: Timeouts and degraded verdicts.
prose.text: {{timeout}} {{strict-verdict-errormsg}} The README describes a wider check {{divergence:strict-verdict-scope}}. Shared behavior is in [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.aws]].

checks.do: That prompt_from and response_from read the same fields the handler reads; the default extractors take the first non-empty string from a fixed key list.
For an asynchronous event source, that a block raises (the default) rather than returning a value, so Lambda's retry and dead-letter handling applies.
That the function timeout covers the handler plus two scans of up to the scan timeout each.

boundary.statement: The decorator scans the extracted prompt before the handler body runs, so a blocked prompt never reaches the handler or its model, and scans the handler's returned text before Lambda returns it; model and tool calls inside the handler are not seen.

quotes: 1. the inbound prompt is scanned by Zscaler AI Guard *before* the handler body runs
2. the handler's response is scanned *before* Lambda returns it to the caller
**Blind below the boundary.** Model calls, tool calls, and agent loops inside the handler are invisible;

default-extractors.statement: The default extractors parse an API Gateway or ALB proxy body as JSON (base64-decoded when flagged; a flagged body that does not decode to UTF-8 is unscannable), fall back to the raw body when it is not JSON, and take the first non-empty string among `prompt`, `message`, `input`, `query`, `question`, `text` for the prompt and `response`, `completion`, `output`, `answer`, `reply`, `message`, `text` for the response.

quotes: return raw if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip() else None

The default extractors understand API Gateway (REST and HTTP APIs), ALB proxy events, and plain direct-invoke payloads: they parse the JSON body (base64-decoded when the envelope flags it, on **both** legs;

a flagged body that does not decode to UTF-8 text -- gzip, images, any binary media type -- is reported unscannable and follows `on_unscannable` instead of being scanned as its base64 wrapper) and take the first non-empty string among

error-results-skipped.statement: A handler result with a `statusCode` of 400 or more is not scanned (the decorator treats it as the handler's own error path), and a custom extractor can return `SKIP` to pass a leg deliberately; otherwise an empty extraction follows `on_unscannable`, blocking by default.

quotes: return _SKIP  # the handler's own error path carries no model output
# Public alias: return SKIP from a custom prompt_from/response_from to say
if isinstance(result, dict) and "statusCode" in result:

evidence.after: elif not isinstance(extracted, str) or not extracted.strip():

response-leg-content.statement: The response scan sends the response text together with the prompt, and with any `context_from` grounding text and `code_response_from` text, joined into one `content` string with direction OUT; the prompt scan can likewise carry `code_prompt_from` text.

transaction-request-id.statement: The transaction ID is the Lambda request ID (`context.aws_request_id`), else a fresh uuid4, so a scan matches a CloudWatch request; a `session_id_from` value is written to the log line.

quotes: so a scan in the AI Guard Console matches a request in CloudWatch one-to-one

no-truncation.statement: Content is sent as-is without truncation; if the API rejects an oversized payload the leg follows `on_error`, blocking by default.

quotes: **Large payloads are not truncated.** Content is sent to AI Guard as-is; if the API rejects an oversized payload the result follows `on_error` (blocked, by default).

block-shapes.statement: By default an HTTP proxy event (recognized from envelope keys such as `httpMethod`, `routeKey`, `requestContext.http` or `requestContext.elb`, even without a body) gets a 403 JSON response naming the leg, severity, policy and detectors, and every other event raises `AIGuardBlocked`; the README's reason is that an asynchronous source treats a returned value as success and would delete the blocked message. An `on_block` callable replaces both.

quotes: or "elb" in ctx                          # ALB target group
# Non-HTTP events (direct invoke, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, ...): raise, so
because an async event source treats any returned value as success and would silently delete the blocked message
or "http" in ctx                         # HTTP API (v2) / Function URL

an HTTP API
    (payload format 2.0) or Function URL event omits "body" entirely on a
    bodyless request -- a GET route, an OPTIONS preflight, an empty POST -- and
    those still have to receive the 403
"message": "Request blocked by Zscaler AI Guard (%s scan)." % leg,

timeout.statement: With no `timeout=` argument the scan timeout is `AIGUARD_TIMEOUT`, else 30 seconds, read once when the handler is decorated; the README sizes a Lambda timeout as handler time plus two scans.

quotes: # None means "take AIGUARD_TIMEOUT", resolved once at decoration time.
Size the Lambda timeout for handler time plus two scans;

strict-verdict-errormsg.statement: Under `strict_verdict=True` the decorator rejects an allow verdict only when it carries an `errorMsg`; it reads no other degradation signal from the verdict.

quotes: if error is None and strict_verdict and action == "allow" and verdict.get("error_msg"):

strict-verdict-scope.summary: What strict_verdict treats as a degraded scan in the Lambda decorator.

positions.says: The README says strict_verdict rejects a verdict whose detection services report trouble: timeout or error flags, an error or timeout category, or a populated per-service errors array.

quotes: a verdict whose detection services report trouble (the `timeout`/`error` flags, an `error`/`timeout` category, or a populated per-service `errors` array)

positions.says: The code checks only whether an allow verdict carries errorMsg; its verdict parser keeps no timeout, error or errors field.

quotes: if error is None and strict_verdict and action == "allow" and verdict.get("error_msg"):

strict-verdict-scope.impact: A degraded scan that reports trouble only through per-detector fields passes as allow even under strict_verdict.
